:::{#thm-deriv-matrix-product-vector}

#### Vector-derivative of a product of matrices

If $\matr{A}$ ($\ell \times m$) and $\matr{B}$ ($m \times q$)
are constant with respect to $\vcoef$,
and $\vecf{v} = \vecf{v}(\vcoef)$ is a $q \times 1$ vector
that depends on the $p \times 1$ vector $\vcoef$,
then:

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef} (\matr{A} \matr{B} \vecf{v})}_{p \times \ell} =
\underbrace{\paren{\deriv{\vcoef} \vecf{v}}}_{p \times q}
\underbrace{\tp{\matr{B}}}_{q \times m}
\underbrace{\tp{\matr{A}}}_{m \times \ell}
$$

:::

::: proof

Apply @thm-deriv-matrix-vector
with the constant $\ell \times q$ matrix $\matr{A}\matr{B}$,
then use the [transpose of a product](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-transpose-product):

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vcoef} (\matr{A} \matr{B} \vecf{v})
&= \paren{\deriv{\vcoef} \vecf{v}} \tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})}
&& \text{(derivative of a matrix-vector product)}
\\
&= \paren{\deriv{\vcoef} \vecf{v}} \tp{\matr{B}}\,\tp{\matr{A}}
&& \text{(transpose of a product)}
\ea
$$

:::

:::{#exm-deriv-matrix-product-vector}

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$ ($1 \times 2$),
$\matr{B} = \begin{pmatrix}2 & 0 \\
0 & 3\end{pmatrix}$ ($2 \times 2$),
and $\vecf{v}(\vcoef) = \vcoef$ where $\vcoef = \tp{(\coef{1}, \coef{2})}$.
Then $\matr{A}\matr{B}\vecf{v} = 2\coef{1}$, and:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef}(\matr{A}\matr{B}\vecf{v})}_{2 \times 1}
&= \underbrace{\paren{\deriv{\vcoef}\vcoef}}_{2 \times 2}
\underbrace{\tp{\matr{B}}}_{2 \times 2}
\underbrace{\tp{\matr{A}}}_{2 \times 1} \\
&= \matr{I}_2
\begin{pmatrix}2 & 0 \\
0 & 3\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1 \\
0\end{pmatrix} \\
&= \begin{pmatrix}2 \\
0\end{pmatrix}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
